provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Ext family batch. Aimed at independent window and door installers, not dealer-supplied sites. No window, glass or door brands named; energy terms are generic. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Double-hung, casement, slider, picture, awning, bay and bow windows, which suits kitchens, bedrooms and stairwells, and which ones open for cleaning from inside
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners know the room, not the window name. A guide by room gets them to a style before the estimate visit.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Vinyl, fiberglass, wood, wood-clad and aluminium frames compared by upkeep, colour inside and out, sightlines and how each handles the local climate
pageStructurePlus.why: Frame material sets most of the price. Buyers who understand the trade-off accept the quote instead of shopping it.

pageStructurePlus.section: Glass packages and energy labels explained
pageStructurePlus.contains: Double versus triple pane, low-E coatings, gas fills, reading the energy label, U-factor and solar heat gain in plain words, noise-reducing glass
pageStructurePlus.why: Glass is the most confusing line on a window quote. Plain answers stop the 'is the cheaper one the same?' call.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Fiberglass, steel and wood entry doors, sidelights and transoms, hinged versus sliding patio doors, storm doors, and keyed or smart locksets
pageStructurePlus.why: Door buyers decide on looks first. A gallery by style keeps entry door jobs from going to the big-box store.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Pocket inserts versus full tear-out, when interior trim is disturbed, rotted sills, install-day prep inside the house, and old window disposal
pageStructurePlus.why: Two quotes for the same window can differ by the install method. Explaining it is how an installer justifies the better job.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Basement and bedroom egress windows, window wells, tempered glass near doors and tubs, permits and inspections for new openings
pageStructurePlus.why: Egress work is permit-driven and often urgent for a basement finish or a sale. A clear page captures those jobs.

designDirections.name: Clear Quote
designDirections.bestFor: Independent window and door installers who win on a quick measure and an honest price
designDirections.headlineSample: Window replacement and entry doors in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Indigo on white and a neutral grotesque feel like a clean quote. The page pushes the measure request and the call button.

designDirections.name: Brighter Rooms
designDirections.bestFor: Window and door companies with before-and-after rooms and facades to show by style
designDirections.headlineSample: New windows and doors, measured and installed in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. Evergreen and a refined serif suit a considered purchase, and the before-after hero shows foggy old sashes beside clear new glass.

designDirections.name: Framed View
designDirections.bestFor: Installers of wood and fiberglass windows, steel-look patio doors and statement entry doors for custom and older homes
designDirections.headlineSample: Architectural windows and entry doors for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: A gallery-white ground and a Didone display let large windows and door hardware carry the page, like a showroom with nothing to sell but the view.

openers.line: Your Google listing has hours and a phone but no website, so someone with drafty windows can't see a single install of yours before deciding who to invite in to measure.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a window and door site behind that button looks like: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing's website link opens Facebook. A homeowner choosing between casement and double-hung windows needs a style guide and a measure request, not a feed.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest window or door job there.
openers.linkLine: A window page with a style guide and measure request: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site looks like the supplier's template, the same window pages every dealer gets. It never says what makes your install crew different, which is the part people are paying for.
openers.hook: Open the site and check whether it matches other dealers' sites word for word. Note the giveaway, a stock gallery or a manufacturer's footer.
openers.linkLine: A window and door site that's yours, not the supplier's: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your window gallery thumbnails overlap and the call button sits under the menu. People price replacement windows from the couch with their phones.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note exactly what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your window and door site rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to ask you for a window quote except calling. Plenty of homeowners count their windows at night and would rather send the count and the rooms than leave a voicemail.
openers.hook: Check the listing, social pages and any site for a form. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A measure request that asks window count, rooms and door type: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your entry door installs on Instagram are sharp, especially the ones with sidelights. They're buried between reposts when a door gallery by style would sell the next one.
openers.hook: Pick two door or window jobs on their grid you could name by style. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your door and window jobs, sorted by style: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews talk about windows that finally stopped the draft and an installer who vacuumed up after. That's the proof a window buyer wants, and it never leaves your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about drafts, noise or cleanup. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Those window reviews beside the installs they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: The first cold snap is when people feel every drafty window in the house. The window installers they can find online in October fill their install calendar before winter.
openers.hook: Use in late summer or early fall, or late spring for heat-driven markets. Name the season in the reply.

openers.line: A broken patio door or a kicked-in entry door can't wait till morning. When that call to a door installer goes to voicemail, the homeowner books whoever picks up.
openers.hook: Only if they do repairs or board-ups. Call after hours and note whether it hits a full or generic voicemail.
openers.linkLine: A door and glass repair request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your hiring post for a window installer will get read by people who then look you up. A page with your finished window and door jobs tells a good tech the work is steady.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a sign on the van. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A window company page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: You install windows across {City} and nearby towns, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you'll come measure. 'Window replacement' plus the town is the search.
openers.hook: Find the towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the one furthest from their shop.
openers.linkLine: A window and door page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer payment plans on windows, or help with energy rebate paperwork, that belongs on a page. A whole-house window job is a number people want split up first.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing or rebates in posts, reviews or on the van. Otherwise skip.
openers.linkLine: Window financing and rebate help explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: Pulling old sashes out of a pre-war house stirs up lead paint dust, and careful buyers know it. Your registry entry and lead-safe card belong on the window page they read before calling.
openers.hook: Check the state contractor registry and any lead-safe certification they mention. Note that a record exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence and lead-safe window work on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your window jobs come from past customers telling friends how quiet the house got. Those friends still search the window company before they call.
openers.hook: Look for reviews like 'my sister recommended' or 'did our neighbour's windows'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a window referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is tidy window work, straight casings and clean caulk lines. A job like that should lead the page, not sit under a week of posts.
openers.hook: Pick the newest window or door install on their grid and name it: style, frame colour, and the street if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That window job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is tidy work, straight casings and clean caulk lines.

I searched for window installers in {City} and found {Business Name} on social but no site with a style guide or a way to request a measure. I put together a sample window and door page to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got buried. Here's the sample window and door site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a window style guide by room, a plain-words glass and energy page, an entry door gallery and a measure request that asks for window count. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for window and door installers here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a window style guide, a glass explainer, a door gallery and a measure request, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many style and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For an installer your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than a few windows installed."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, Tuesday or Thursday?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before the cold-weather calls."

objections.objection: My window supplier gives me a dealer site already.
objections.handler: "Keep the dealer listing. That site sells their windows; it doesn't say anything about your install crew, your town or your reviews. Yours sells you."

objections.objection: Most of my jobs come from referrals.
objections.handler: "Then the work speaks for itself. A referral still searches your name, and right now they find a Facebook page. The site is where they decide to book the measure."

objections.objection: The big window companies outspend me on adverts.
objections.handler: "They do. Plenty of people sit through the in-home pitch and then look for a local installer with fair prices. That's who your site is for."

objections.objection: People only care about the cheapest window.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the ones comparing glass packages and install methods. Once they see why full-frame costs more, your quote makes sense."

objections.objection: My nephew can build me a site.
objections.handler: "Good, that's cheaper than me. Happy to hand over the style guide and the measure form. If it stalls before fall, the offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a style guide, a door gallery, a measure form and a few town pages. Less than one small window order."

email.subject: Window and door site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for window and door installers in {City}, and I made a sample one for {Business Name} with a style guide and measure request. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} window and door demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to keep it up? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, the first cold snap is coming and drafty-window calls pick up right after. Thought of you.

The window site is still here, same price as before. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a handful of installed windows, not an hourly rate.
Price the measure request higher when it collects window count, rooms, styles and door type.
Style guide, frame comparison and glass explainer are separate lines; each answers a different stage of the decision.
Only quote the egress page for installers who cut new openings and pull permits.
For dealer-network installers, price the migration off the supplier template as its own line.
Door galleries scale with how many door styles they actually install; don't build pages for doors they don't sell.

lineItems.description: Max with a comparison table, room suggestions and a gallery of installs in that style or frame.

lineItems.item: Measure request with count, rooms and door fields
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload of the worst windows, a rebate question and routing to two estimators.
Max with simple diagrams and climate-specific glass suggestions for their region.
Max when it covers entry, patio and storm doors with lockset and glass options filtered by style.
Max when it includes local code notes, window well options and a basement-finish request form.

lineItems.item: Move off the supplier's dealer template
lineItems.description: Max when there are many dealer pages to redirect and their reviews and jobs need moving across.
Max when each town page shows local installs and notes on common house ages and window types there.

whatElseYouSell.name: Inside-and-out window photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Half a day shooting new windows from the street and from inside the brighter rooms, plus your best entry doors, fills the gallery and a season of posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or the week they finish a whole-house window job.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for window and door installs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every week a finished window or door install goes on your Google profile with the style and the town named, so the map listing stays current."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review texts the day after the window install
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The morning after an install, when the house is quieter and warmer, the homeowner gets a text asking how the window crew did."

whatElseYouSell.name: Energy rebate season campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When utility or tax rebates for efficient windows change, a short page and past-customer email explain it plainly and point to your measure request."
whatElseYouSell.when: Whenever rebate rules change, or ahead of fall.

whatElseYouSell.name: Van wrap and yard sign artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A window install van sits in a driveway all day. A clean wrap and a 'new windows by' yard sign with the site on them turn the street into estimates."

whatElseYouSell.name: Neighbour postcards after each window job
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Houses on a street usually got their windows the same year. A postcard showing the neighbour's new windows lands with people who have the same drafts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once there are installs on the site.

whatElseYouSell.name: Drafty-window fall campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short fall push to past estimates and local groups catches people the week they feel the first draft by the window."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in August, run in September and October.

withoutAI.route: Siding crews who open the walls
withoutAI.pitchLine: "A re-side is the cheapest moment to swap windows, and you already work with a siding crew. They need the same before-and-after site you have."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Window and siding jobs are scheduled together, so the introduction is warm.

withoutAI.whoPays: The painter or carpenter, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "After full-frame window installs, someone paints and trims the openings. The carpenter you call needs a site, and they send window jobs back."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Interior finish follows every full-frame job; easy two-way referrals.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your window distributor supplies every independent installer around here and has a catalogue for a site. Introduce me and I'll build their installer map."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Distributors have budgets and their installer list is your next prospect list.

withoutAI.route: Locksmiths who fit new entry doors
withoutAI.whoPays: The locksmith, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Locksmiths rekey and upgrade locks on every new entry door you hang. They need a site, and they hear about broken doors first."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Locksmiths get the break-in calls; door installers get the replacements. A natural loop.

withoutAI.route: Basement finishers who need egress windows
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every basement bedroom needs an egress window, and basement remodelers already call you to cut them. Their site needs the same care yours got."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Basement remodelers sell bigger jobs and buy websites on the same logic.

withoutAI.route: Energy auditors who flag leaky windows
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Energy auditors point at windows in every report. They need a plain site to book audits, and your window page is their next step."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Auditors refer window work constantly and buy credibility.

withAI.route: Quote builder for the window distributor's installers
withAI.pitchLine: "Installers enter rough openings and styles and get a priced window and door order from the distributor, with sizes checked."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties installers to one distributor's pricing, which beats a rebate.

withAI.route: Audit report explainer for energy auditors
withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant turns a dense energy audit into a one-page summary for the homeowner, with window and door fixes listed plainly."
withAI.whyItWorks: Clear reports book more follow-up work, which goes to the window client.

withAI.route: Lockout and break-in intake for locksmiths
withAI.pitchLine: "Late-night lockout and break-in calls get answered, sorted by urgency and booked, and damaged doors are flagged for your window and door client."
withAI.whyItWorks: Locksmiths lose night calls; the door installer gets the replacements.

withAI.pitchLine: "The basement crew you cut egress windows for loses quotes to slow callbacks. The same follow-up texts, set up for them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Configuration of something already built, with a warm referral.

withAI.pitchLine: "Maintenance staff snap each rental's windows and doors at turnover, and an assistant flags broken seals, cracked glass and failing locks for one installer."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers need turnover records anyway, and the window client gets steady repair work.

withAI.route: HOA window and door style checker
withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant checks replacement window grid patterns and door colours against HOA rules before the request reaches the board."
withAI.whyItWorks: Resubmissions waste a month; managers pay to stop them.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for window quotes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "While you're setting a window, missed callers get a text asking how many windows or which door, so the callback is a booking, not a phone tag."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Window price range tool by count and style
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners pick how many windows, which styles and frame material, and see a range before the measure visit. Tyre-kickers looking for builder-grade sort themselves out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price per window by style and frame, door prices and install adders.

softwareAI.name: Order deposit and install balance billing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Windows are custom-ordered, so the deposit goes out at signing and the balance at install, both automatic with a card link and a lead-time note."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Order lead-time updates to customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Custom windows take weeks. Customers get a text when the order is placed, when it ships and when the install date is set, and stop calling to ask."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their order stages and typical lead times.

softwareAI.name: Replies to window and door reviews
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone writes that the bedroom is finally quiet; a reply naming the windows and the room is drafted for your thumbs-up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review texts. Needs a dozen past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Rough-opening measure sheet app
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The measurer enters each opening's width, height and style on a tablet, and the window order sheet builds itself with no retyping from paper."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their measure sheet and order form.

softwareAI.name: Window and door job board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Measures, orders, deliveries and install days for every window job on one board, so nothing sits in a supplier's backlog unnoticed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their stages, supplier list and who measures.

softwareAI.name: Window count and style draft from house photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner uploads street-side shots and it drafts the window count and styles per wall, so the first call already has a ballpark."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past jobs with counts to test against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; a person always confirms at the measure.

softwareAI.name: Glass and style chatbot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'casement or double-hung for the kitchen' and 'is triple pane worth it here' at midnight, from your notes, and books the window measure."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their style and glass notes and current lead times. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Window warranty and service log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every window and door installed is logged with its order number and warranty terms, so a failed seal years later is a five-minute claim."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past orders and install dates.

softwareAI.name: Door style preview on the customer's front
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a shot of the front of the house and see entry door styles, colours and sidelights in place before ordering."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the door styles they sell. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; previews are labelled as previews.

softwareAI.name: Rebate paperwork checklist builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For each window order it lists the energy rebate documents the homeowner needs and fills in the product details, so the rebate actually gets filed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, where rebates apply. Needs current rebate rules for their area.

softwareAI.name: Talk-through measure to window quote
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk room to room saying each window size and style, and a draft window quote in your format is waiting in the van."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their quote template and pricing. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Supplier order error checker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before an order goes to the window supplier, it compares sizes, handing and grid patterns against the measure sheet and flags anything odd."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the measure sheet app first. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with order status
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner sees their window and door order, signed styles, delivery status and install date in one place."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the job board running first.

softwareAI.name: Installer checklist app with sill and flashing steps
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Installers tick off sill pan, flashing tape, foam and interior trim per opening, with a shot each, so every window is installed the same way."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they run two crews. Needs their install standard.

softwareAI.name: Profit by window style and install type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether inserts or full-frame jobs, vinyl or fiberglass windows, actually earn more once crew hours and trim work are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of orders and crew hours.

softwareAI.name: Seal-failure check reminders to past customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each fall, past window customers get a note on spotting fogged glass or sticking sashes, with a service request link and a door upgrade offer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a customer list with install dates.

softwareAI.name: Window page writer by style and town
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new window style or town page every month, drafted from your installs and notes, approved by you before it goes live."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs job notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Window installer hiring screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say whether they've done full-frame window installs, trim work and lead-safe jobs, so you only phone the ones worth meeting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: When they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the window price range tool
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a window price range tool for one installer. Every independent window company gets 'roughly how much per window' all day."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the build and taught you the pricing.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Installer locator for a window distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who've decided on new windows still ask your counter staff who can install them. A searchable list of the independents on your account answers that and keeps their orders with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors already spend on installer loyalty.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Independent dealer site program for a window maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your window dealers all run the same template with no local proof. A program that gives each dealer a real site with its own window installs beats the copy-paste."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund dealer marketing; you know what an installer site needs.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Window and door association member kit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member window installers a template with a style guide and measure request as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One deal reaches many window owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with a window installer client start blank. License my window template with the glass explainer and measure request."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell the finished part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each window territory needs its own town pages and a measure request that routes to the right owner."
"Rebate programs list approved window contractors in a spreadsheet. A searchable contractor page with rebate steps helps homeowners finish the process."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Programs need participation; you already know the window contractor side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: New-home window and door upgrade selector
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New-home buyers pick window grids and front door upgrades online, and the selections route to one installer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders like upgrade revenue; the window client becomes default.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Owners of older homes need to know when to restore a wood window and when to replace. A directory of local window restorers serves them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Preservation groups fund homeowner guidance and value trade expertise.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly note on window and door lead times by type, built from what installers report, so quotes promise realistic dates."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Built only from contributed data, it never claims more than installers share.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A window company in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "My window and door clients get their town to themselves. Once {City} is settled, I pitch the strongest independent window shop two cities over."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusive geography reuses the window template and demo.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue window sites stuck on dead templates
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Dropped from a dealer program, or left with a half-built window site? I can move it to one you own in a couple of weeks."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Installers who lose a dealer site need a replacement fast and have already decided to buy.

upsellLadder.offer: Window and door site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The window site and care plan go on one contract, so a new door style or lead time update is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review texts the day after the window install
upsellLadder.trigger: The first window job installed since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "That family who just got new windows is your next review. Let's ask the morning after every install."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention customers calling to ask when windows will arrive.
upsellLadder.line: "Those 'where are my windows' calls stop when the texts go out on their own."

upsellLadder.offer: Window price range tool by count and style
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of measure requests show the same counts and styles asked again and again.
upsellLadder.line: "Most window requests ask about the same few double-hung sizes. The range tool answers them before the visit."

upsellLadder.trigger: The window gallery still shows marked placeholders, or a striking whole-house job finishes.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot your best window and door jobs from inside and out in one morning."

upsellLadder.trigger: A window order arrives wrong because of a retyped measurement.
upsellLadder.line: "That wrong-size window cost a week. Measurements typed once, on site, stop it."

upsellLadder.trigger: They add a second install crew or a second measurer.
upsellLadder.line: "Two window crews need one board for orders and install days. Let's set it up."
